excerpt: Sill shows a window from your Mac, or its whole desktop, on your iPhone or iPad, and lets you use it with touch, a keyboard or Apple Pencil.
taps and clicks, scrolls with momentum, the on-screen trackpad, keys and typed text, and Apple Pencil as the pointer.
Three fingers swipe and pinch as on a Mac's trackpad: Mission Control, App Exposé, the Spaces, Apps and Show Desktop
A keyboard attached to your device types on your Mac as soon as the picture shows, Esc included
text you copy on your Mac is ready to paste on your device, and Paste in Sill sends what you copied on your device to your Mac's clipboard
The menus of the app you use reach your device too: in the iPad's own menu bar on iPadOS 26 or later, and behind the Menus button in Sill's bar.
"Launch any Mac app." Sill's Apps list on an iPad held sideways, with a search field, the apps open now and every app installed on the Mac.
"Every window, one tap away." On an iPad held sideways, a window's thumbnail held in Sill's bar shows Close, Minimize and Full Screen.
Aa on your device resizes the window you stream on your Mac, through Accessibility, so its text shows at the size you pick
The virtual display (off by default) moves a window you stream onto a display of its own on your Mac, so it keeps updating when other windows cover it.
"Laptop mode." An iPad held upright, with the Mac's Clock app on top and Sill's bar, a row of keys and a trackpad below it.
Larger Picture, in the settings panel, gives a window's picture the room of the window thumbnails, down to where the keyboard comes up
half open like a laptop, the picture is above the fold with a trackpad and keys below; closed, Sill runs on the cover display.
When someone moves the mouse at your Mac, your device shows the pointer where it is.
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
Away from home, Sill starts at a quality a slower connection can carry, and when you get home, the session moves to your network by itself.
Direct Wireless Connection lets an iPhone or iPad near your Mac connect without a shared Wi-Fi network, the way AirDrop does.
Over a USB cable, the two pair by themselves.
Each iPhone or iPad pairs with your Mac once. After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
Sill's Settings › Devices on your Mac lists the devices you paired. Remove one you no longer use, or have lost.
To forget one Mac you paired, touch and hold its row on the connect screen and choose Forget.
Pick a lower Quality in the settings panel on your iPhone or iPad, or in the Sill menu on your Mac.
Sill for Mac notices that it is holding frames back and tells your device, which says so over the picture and, in its Settings, offers a quality the link can carry.
Sill doesn't update itself, but it tells you when a new version is out: its menu and Settings say so, with a link to the release.
Unless you turn off “Check for updates automatically” in Sill’s Settings › General, once a day it asks GitHub (api.github.com) whether a newer version of Sill has been released
There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
On your Mac, choose Show Log… in the Sill menu, or open the Sill folder in Library/Logs in your home folder.
brew install --cask saffsanity/sill/sill in Terminal installs the same Sill.dmg from Sill’s own tap. To update it, quit Sill and run brew upgrade --cask sill.
open Terminal, type shasum -a 256 and a space, drag Sill.dmg into the window and press Return. It should print the same SHA-256 as the release’s notes on GitHub
This builds Sill.app with SwiftPM, signs it with your Apple Development identity, replaces /Applications/Sill.app and opens it.
`swift run -c release SillHost` runs the same host on the command line... With `--synthetic` it streams a test pattern with no Screen Recording needed.
In the Sill target's Signing & Capabilities, pick your team, and change the bundle identifier `me.saffer.sill` to one of your own.
